name: Nergal-Sharezer
title: Babylonian officer at the fall of Jerusalem
summary: Nergal-Sharezer was a high-ranking Babylonian officer who took part in the siege and conquest of Jerusalem in 586 BC under King Nebuchadnezzar. He is mentioned in the book of Jeremiah as one of the Babylonian officials who stationed themselves at the city gate after it fell. He is often identified with Neriglissar, who later became king of Babylon (560–556 BC).

keyEvents.title: The Siege of Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Nergal-Sharezer was among the Babylonian officers who participated in the long siege of Jerusalem, which led to the city's fall in 586 BC.

keyEvents.title: The Entry into Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: After the city walls were breached, the Babylonian commanders entered the city. Nergal-Sharezer was among those who stationed themselves at the Middle Gate as a sign of conquest and takeover.

keyEvents.title: King Zedekiah's Flight and Capture
keyEvents.description: When the Babylonian officers, including Nergal-Sharezer, entered Jerusalem, King Zedekiah fled during the night but was captured on the plains of Jericho and taken to Nebuchadnezzar.

keyEvents.title: The Release of the Prophet Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: Nebuchadnezzar ordered that the prophet Jeremiah be treated well. Nergal-Sharezer was among the Babylonian officers involved in the process of bringing Jeremiah out of the guardhouse and ensuring his safety.

keyEvents.title: The Destruction of Jerusalem's Temple and Walls
keyEvents.description: As part of the Babylonian military leadership, Nergal-Sharezer contributed to the total destruction of Jerusalem, including the temple and city walls, which marked the beginning of the exile.
